DTE.summary: DTE Energy is a regulated utility company serving Michigan, and it has been getting modest attention on social media. In the past 24 hours, Reddit mentions were 82, down slightly from 99 the previous day, ranking 8th on the Reddit list. On Stocktwits, bullish sentiment is strong with 15 bullish tags and only 1 bearish tag. The messages show a community that views DTE as a stable, dividend-paying utility with growth potential. One user highlighted that Michigan regulators approved DTE's 20-year power contracts for Google's 1-gigawatt data center near Detroit, known as Project Cannoli. This is seen as a positive development because Google will pay a minimum billing demand of 80% of contracted capacity, providing a steady revenue stream. Another user noted that DTE has a monopoly on electricity in its service territory, which is a classic utility advantage. Several commenters are buying shares regularly, with one aiming for a price of $140 and looking forward to the dividend on the 15th. The mention of Sir Peter Thiel's energy portfolio also sparked some interest, though DTE was just one of several tickers listed. Overall, the tone is bullish but low-key, typical of utility stock discussions. Investors should know that DTE is a regulated utility, meaning its earnings are relatively stable and it pays a solid dividend. The Google data center deal is a significant catalyst, as it aligns with the growing demand for electricity from tech companies. However, utilities are sensitive to interest rates, and higher rates can make their dividends less attractive. Also, regulatory decisions can impact profitability. The community seems to be accumulating shares for the long haul, with little day-trading chatter. The low number of bearish tags suggests confidence. Risks include potential regulatory changes, rising costs, and the possibility that the data center deal may not materialize as expected. But for income-oriented investors, DTE offers a reliable dividend and exposure to the electrification trend. The discussion is not overly hyped, which is typical for a utility stock.

ASTS.summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) is generating a lot of buzz in online communities, with Reddit mentions jumping from 53 to 72 in the last 24 hours, placing it at rank 9 among all stocks discussed. On Stocktwits, the sentiment is overwhelmingly bullish, with 36 bullish tags versus only 8 bearish tags. The conversation is dominated by excitement over recent developments that supporters say validate the company's long-term vision. A key theme is the company's growing credibility: users point to major government contracts and partnerships with large communications companies as evidence that ASTS is not just a 'cult stock' but a serious player in the satellite communications space. One popular post highlights that cult stocks don't get major government contracts or partnerships with the biggest communications companies, and they don't have the support to build the world's largest and most sophisticated satellites. Another user shared a timeline of the last five days, suggesting the investment thesis is being rewritten. There's also enthusiasm about the company's decision to use Firefly's Miranda engine for its rockets, with details about extensive testing and performance. The filing of an 8-K and a PCMag article about ASTS building its own rockets to catch up with Starlink Mobile are also driving discussion. Many users express unwavering commitment, with one saying they haven't sold any shares and are only buying more. The bullish sentiment is so strong that some are mocking the bears. However, it's important to note that this is a highly speculative stock with no revenue yet, and the enthusiasm is based on future potential. Investors should be aware of the risks: the company is not yet profitable, faces intense competition from Starlink and others, and execution risks are high. The stock is volatile and heavily influenced by social media sentiment. While the community is very optimistic, the lack of current financial results means the stock is priced on hope and contracts that may take years to materialize. The recent surge in mentions and bullish tags suggests a lot of retail interest, which can lead to sharp price swings. Investors should do their own research and consider the long-term viability of the technology and business model.

SPCX.summary: SPCX is getting a lot of attention on Reddit and Stocktwits, but the conversation is overwhelmingly bullish and a bit chaotic. Over the past 24 hours, Reddit mentions dropped from 93 to 54, yet it still ranks 11th among all tickers discussed. On Stocktwits, bullish tags outnumber bearish ones by more than 10 to 1 (34 bullish vs. 3 bearish), which tells you the crowd is extremely optimistic. The messages themselves are full of rocket emojis, price targets like $300+ by end of year, and claims that SpaceX (which is what SPCX likely refers to, though the ticker itself is unusual) will be the gold standard of space exploration. One user thanked 'commies' for the dip and predicted a $3 trillion market cap, while another celebrated a successful launch. There's also some political noise, with one post referencing President Biden in a crude way, and another tying SPCX to Tesla and Trump-related tickers. The bullishness is driven by excitement about space exploration and Elon Musk's ventures rather than concrete financials. Also, the mention volume is declining, which could mean the hype is cooling off. With such a lopsided sentiment, contrarians might worry that everyone who wants to buy already has. Still, the community is resilient, with users posting about buying the dip and holding for the long term. For a regular investor, the key takeaway is that SPCX is a high-risk, sentiment-driven play. The positive factors center on the space industry's growth potential and Musk's track record, while the negatives include the lack of clear fundamentals, regulatory risks, and the possibility that the ticker doesn't represent direct ownership of SpaceX. As always, do your own research and don't rely solely on social media hype.

Reddit mentions fell from 134 to 54 in the past 24 hours, but it still ranks 12th, showing it remains a hot topic. On Stocktwits, bullish tags (15) outnumber bearish ones (8), but the gap is narrower than for more speculative tickers. The messages are all over the place: some users are hoping for a market reversal, others are thanking or blaming political figures for market moves, and many are simply reaffirming their dollar-cost averaging strategies. For example, one user said they 'dca'ed biweekly' and believe 'the market goes up long term,' while another complained about manipulation and stocks moving in the same direction. There's also a lot of political banter, with references to Trump, Biden, and MAGA, which shows how politicized investing has become. The ETF tracks the S&P 500, so it's diversified and low-cost, making it a favorite for retirement accounts and passive investing. However, the community is clearly anxious about recent volatility, Fed policy, earnings, and midterm elections. Some believe all bad news is priced in and expect a year-end rally, while others are bearish and see manipulation. For a regular investor, VOO offers broad market exposure with minimal effort, but it's not immune to downturns. The positive factors include its low expense ratio, diversification, and the community's faith in long-term growth. The negatives include market-wide risks like inflation, interest rates, and political uncertainty, as well as the tendency for online sentiment to be swayed by short-term noise. Overall, VOO remains a solid core holding, but don't expect the online chatter to provide actionable timing signals.

FLY.summary: Firefly Aerospace ($FLY) is getting a lot of attention on Stocktwits and a sudden spike on Reddit after announcing a massive $1.3 billion, three-year agreement with AST SpaceMobile ($ASTS). The deal covers 36 rocket engines, IP licensing, and engineering support, and investors are clearly excited. Reddit mentions jumped from just 1 to 14 in 24 hours, and Stocktwits sentiment is overwhelmingly bullish with 29 bullish tags versus only 1 bearish. The community sees this as a transformative partnership that could evolve into something even bigger, especially with mentions of the 'golden dome' defense program. Many are comparing it to the early days of the AI boom, where companies invested in each other to build an entire industry. Some are even calculating hypothetical share prices if Firefly reaches a $10 billion, $50 billion, or $100 billion valuation, with one post showing a $1 trillion valuation would imply nearly $6,000 per share. Others are simply saying 'still so cheap' and 'next stop $60+'. The stock is bouncing off recent lows, and the deal comes just ahead of Firefly's November 10 earnings call, where Q2 revenue was $117.7 million, up 45.5% sequentially. However, not everyone is convinced. One user questioned why AST SpaceMobile didn't partner with Rocket Lab ($RKLB) instead, comparing it to GoPro's disastrous drone attempt. There's also concern about the stock being down from its May high in the $60s to around $20 now. But the overall tone is highly optimistic, with many believing the company will get repriced higher. Investors should note the strong bullish sentiment but also be aware that the stock is volatile and the deal's full impact remains to be seen. The partnership could be a game-changer for Firefly's engine business and space economy ambitions, but execution risks and competition are real. Keep an eye on the earnings call for more details.

On the bullish side, many point to the company's strong fundamentals: record Q3 revenue of $909 million, up 28% year-over-year, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.72. Others are buying the dip, expecting a bounce, and believing acquisitions will pay off. The stock broke sharply below its prior range, and some call it the 'worst stock in the market.' Despite the mixed sentiment, the overall tone is cautiously optimistic, with many seeing value at current levels. Investors should weigh the strong revenue growth and market position against the risks of insider selling, execution on acquisitions, and potential delays in federal contracts. The upcoming weeks will be telling as the market digests the Q4 guidance and insider activity.

CSCO.summary:
Cisco Systems ($CSCO) isn't exactly a meme stock, and on Reddit it's practically invisible right now—zero mentions in the last 24 hours. But over on Stocktwits, the conversation is alive and clearly leaning bullish, with 18 bullish tags versus just 2 bearish ones. So what's everyone talking about? The big theme is AI and data center spending. One popular post lumps Cisco in with Broadcom, Oracle, and SpaceX, arguing that no serious businessperson expects data center construction to slow down, and that AI safeguards won't stop the money from flowing. That post got a handful of likes and reposts, and it captures the mood: Cisco is seen as a quiet beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom, not just an old-school networking company.

There's also a lot of chatter about a sharp market selloff. One message describes the Dow plunging 1,800 points, with Nvidia and Cisco under heavy pressure and the Nasdaq down 5.5%. That's clearly a scary headline, but the reaction from Cisco bulls is telling: one simply says '$CSCO overreaction,' implying the drop was unjustified. Another argues that Cisco is 'decent in AI and growing it' but also has earnings power from many other areas, so the selloff is 'way overdone.' A more colorful post calls Cisco 'a killer whale in all things tech not just AI tech' and predicts a return to $120 within weeks. That's the kind of confidence you see when investors think a blue-chip name has been unfairly beaten down.

Not everything is rosy, though. One user warns that networking gear for the 'next hall' is being ordered before the current hall proves it can pay—suggesting that forward orders might be treated as backlog safety, but in a repricing environment, backlog is just future spending that someone can cancel. That's a nuanced bearish point about demand sustainability. Another notes the frustrating relative performance: 'When $QQQ pumps this $CSCO stays flat. When $QQQ sneezes, this dies.' That captures the downside beta problem—Cisco doesn't rally much in good times but gets hit in bad times.

Analyst actions are also in the mix. One post mentions Morgan Stanley downgrading Cisco to equal weight from overweight, which is a negative signal. But another highlights that Ken Fisher's firm added 20% more to its Cisco position in Q3, alongside TLT and UnitedHealth. That's a notable vote of confidence from a well-known fund manager. And then there's the earnings setup: one user says at this price, all Cisco has to do is report in line and reiterate guidance for the stock to go higher, and any margin improvement could trigger a 12-15% pop. That's a classic 'low expectations' bull case.

Overall, the Stocktwits crowd sees Cisco as a value play with AI upside, oversold after a market-wide scare, and poised for a bounce if earnings don't disappoint. The bears worry about backlog quality, relative weakness, and analyst downgrades. With Reddit silent, Stocktwits is the main pulse here, and it's decidedly more bullish than not.
